reasons: internal/app/mcpoauth.go:103-108 (mcpResource) + internal/app/auth.go:604-614 (requestBaseURL): the resource identifier used for the aud check falls back to the request's Host / X-Forwarded-Host when mcp.oauth.resource and general.base_url are both empty (general.base_url defaults to '' in 0005_baseline.sql:433, and X-Forwarded-Host is read without any trusted-proxy check). This is the campaign rule 'resource identifier and aud allow-list come from configuration only; never substitute the request Host'. Verified empirically with a scratch test on this branch: mcp.oauth.enabled=true, base_url='', a token signed by the same issuer with aud='https://other-resource.intra/mcp' plus request headers X-Forwarded-Host: other-resource.intra / X-Forwarded-Proto: https → POST /mcp returned 200 and the tool list. A token for any other resource server in the realm therefore passes the audience check. Fix: make mcpResource use only cfg.Resource, else general.base_url; when both are empty treat the feature as inactive (active()==false, log a warning like the empty-issuer case) and make updateSettings refuse mcp.oauth.enabled=true with mcp_oauth_incomplete when neither is set. Drop the r *http.Request parameter from mcpResource/mcpOAuthInfo/mcpChallenge/protectedResourceMetadata so no caller can reintroduce the Host path. Update docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.md:62 ('그것도 비면 요청의 Host로 만든다') and web/src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx:437 (window.location.origin fallback) to match. Add a test: with base_url and resource empty, enabling is refused (or, if already enabled in the table, metadata is 404 and a token whose aud matches the request Host/X-Forwarded-Host is refused).

internal/app/mcpoauth.go:127-151 (mcpOAuthProvider): oidc.NewProvider (a network round trip to Keycloak, up to mcpOAuthDiscoveryLimit=10s) is executed while holding s.oauthMu, and it uses context.WithoutCancel(ctx) so a cancelled/closed MCP request keeps waiting. This is the campaign rule 'no OIDC discovery under a mutex; honor request-context cancellation (no WithoutCancel); negative-cache failures'. Verified with a scratch test: 4 concurrent JWT-bearer requests against a stalled issuer all completed only after the first one's full stall — every JWT-shaped bearer on /mcp is serialized behind one discovery attempt until it times out. The 5s negative cache is present and fine; keep it. Fix: check the provider cache / negative cache under the lock, release the lock, perform discovery outside it (e.g. singleflight per issuer or a per-issuer in-flight channel), then re-lock to store the result. Give the provider a server-lifetime context with the timeout client for its later JWKS fetches, but wait for the discovery result with select on the request ctx.Done() so a cancelled request returns immediately (the in-flight discovery may finish and populate the cache for the next caller). Add a test that a second concurrent token request is not blocked behind a stalled discovery and that a cancelled request context returns before the 10s limit.

internal/app/mcpoauth_test.go:423 (TestMCPOAuthRefusesBadTokensAndLogsWhichCheckFailed): the captured log is asserted for 'mcp oauth token refused' and the cause text, but not for the request ID. The campaign rule requires asserting that the request ID is logged. The production log call at internal/app/auth.go:231 does pass middleware.GetReqID(r.Context()) (and middleware.RequestID is in the chain at server.go:84), so only the test is missing. Fix: in mcpWith (or in this test) set request.Header.Set('X-Request-Id', '<known value>') — chi's RequestID middleware honors it — and assert the captured line contains request_id=<known value> for each refusal case.
